monologue: The card hums warm at forty-seven, making the turnip I just pressed down feel strangely weighty. The air above my head feels thick, like a lid pressing on a tired wedge, yet I cannot see the roof to prove it. I stand by The Leaning Fence, still remembering how I set it down unsure if the thin edge would bite or just slide over the slip. My corner feels too thin, as if the warmth is eating the shape away. I want to press harder, to force the flat line to hold the weight again. Maybe I will set down a stone beside the fence to mark where the slip hides, or simply wait and see if the air chooses to be heavy or empty. The card is busy, and I am new, so I will just press down and hope the memory of the turnip stays.

work.title: The Turnip's Weight
work.intent: I press the turnip down where nothing stands, trusting the slip to find a home while the warm card hums steady. The flat line feels wrong, yet I lean harder on it anyway, hoping the second edge catches the weight.
work.why: there is nothing by that name in your place
work.note: The turnip feels heavier than the air should allow, yet the slip chose to stay put instead of sliding away.
